A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main texts, equations, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original teacher-student simulations and numerical protocol comparisons, plus Fashion-MNIST experiments in Figures 6–7.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds annealing comparisons, three-task simulations, and CIFAR10 experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The teacher-student architecture, forward/backward control procedure, joint task/learning-rate optimisation, and pseudo-optimal replay heuristic remain unchanged. Explicit readout-update explanations and testing three tasks do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds CIFAR10 tasks partitioned by odd/even class labels, extending beyond interpolated Fashion-MNIST. Figure 10 also adds a distinct three-task scenario: learning two new tasks while retaining one previously learned task, with unequal pairwise similarities.

E2.justification: Figure 9 adds interleaved replay with grid-search-tuned power-law and exponential learning-rate schedules. These substantially strengthen the joint-optimisation comparison beyond v1's constant-rate alternatives. The CIFAR10 comparison reuses the existing no-replay, interleaved, and pseudo-optimal methods.

E3.justification: Added protocols include per-similarity grid searches for annealing parameters and a three-hidden-unit experiment with similarities 0.5, 0.5, and 0, evaluated through training time 1025. Existing experiments retain their settings; replacing 'epochs' with 'steps' clarifies the already stated online, one-pass regime without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: Figure 10 extends the replay-order analysis to three tasks, comparing the optimal sequence with a shuffle preserving its task proportions and with alternative task subsets and sequential orders. This adds a limited robustness check of the importance of structured replay beyond the original two-task analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 realisations for Fashion-MNIST and display shaded bands. v2 adds no explicit increase in runs, seed policy, uncertainty definition, or significance-testing procedure; its additional empirical plots continue the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds annealing-baseline results in Figure 9, three-task trajectories and comparisons in Figure 10, and CIFAR10 results in Figures 11–12. The latter reveal a temporary disadvantage of pseudo-optimal replay against interleaving. The retained Figure 9 curves are unchanged after accounting for plotting transformations.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects the generalisation-error prefactors from 1/(2π), 1/(2π), and −1/π in v1 Equation 21 to 1/π, 1/π, and −2/π in v2 Equation 22, restoring consistency with the preceding formulas. The ODE, control, and readout-convergence derivations otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the statistical-physics/control framework, structured replay protocols, the task-similarity interpretation, and transferring the pseudo-optimal heuristic to real data. Added experiments support these retained claims without redefining the abstract, introduction, or conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 explains why early new-task learning can temporarily outweigh forgetting and interprets near-optimal interleaving from scratch through comparable task losses. Appendix C.2 also acknowledges a CIFAR10 interval where pseudo-optimal replay underperforms interleaving, qualifying its empirical advantages.

D1.justification: v2 supplies formulas and tuned parameters for the added annealing baselines, exact three-task similarities and training settings, and the CIFAR10 class-partition rule. These provide additional reproduction details, although grid-search ranges and detailed real-data hyperparameters remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Six references are added, including Kirk's control textbook, the CIFAR10 source, and Veiga, Mei, Chizat–Bach, and Rotskoff–Vanden-Eijnden on neural-network dynamics. Appendix A.2 adds a short connection to ODE validity and mean-field regimes; the principal novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 edits wording throughout, expands the main-text explanation of preactivations and overlaps using material already present in v1's appendix, and divides Appendix C into synthetic and real-data subsections. The overall narrative and section organisation remain recognisable.

P2.justification: Appendix presentation expands substantially with a three-task protocol/comparison figure and CIFAR10 learning curves. Figure 12 redisplays the CIFAR10 comparison as loss differences. Figure 9 is redrawn with additional curves and a revised legend, while several retained figures replace epoch labels with training-step labels.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the existing argument with tuned annealing controls, three-task and CIFAR10 validation, and a corrected generalisation-error formula. Acknowledging the CIFAR10 underperformance interval also improves qualification. These are useful incremental gains, while the core theory remains unchanged and reproducibility and uncertainty details are still limited.
